what: Sales tools someone should build: Rotten Tomatoes for sales advice (guru scored on actual quota), Carfax for job offers (how many reps held seat + hit rate), Zillow for territories, TurboTax for commission, Find My for ghosted prospects, Rocket Money for unused sales stack.
why_us: High-engagement list of concrete, monetizable gaps in B2B sales stack. Sales pros already pay heavily for tools; these are verification/transparency layers on top of existing spend.
revenue: Potential $20-50/mo per user or team seats; high willingness from sales orgs.

what: twinhoods: AI website that translates cities into ones you already know (e.g. Seattle via Istanbul neighborhoods). Launched after 10-year personal pain. Users vote cities to add.
why_us: Classic 'I wish there was an app' turned into shipped AI product with strong launch traction. Shows demand for hyper-personalized, culturally fluent tools.
revenue: Early launch, not disclosed yet; viral potential from travel/expat audience.

what: GodsView AI crossed $6,000 MRR. 69k+ registered users, 20k email subs, first iOS app launched. Built from idea in a few months by solo/small team.
why_us: Concrete micro-SaaS AI revenue proof. Clear path from idea → users → MRR without massive funding.

what: beehiiv crossed $3m MRR. $0→$1M in 36 months, $1M→$2M in 16, $2M→$3M in 9 months. Now adding ~$100k MRR every 2.5 weeks. Owned audiences as the engine.
why_us: Elite growth case for creator/newsletter infrastructure. Shows acceleration when distribution is owned vs algorithmic.

what: Context layer for consumers: personal preferences, history, relationships and taste owned by the user and open to any AI agent/product. Enterprises are getting this; individuals are not. Currently re-explained to every new AI tool.
why_us: Privacy + personalization gap. High long-term value as AI agents proliferate. Users would pay for control of their own context.
revenue: Subscription or one-time personal data vault; B2C + API to agents.

what: AI presentation tools (Gamma and similar) heavily criticized: expensive ($12-90/mo), AI doesn't follow instructions, exports overflow/break, every deck looks the same, recommends Canva instead. Users call it waste of money.
why_us: Clear pain in AI design/presentation space. Opportunity for cheaper, more controllable, or specialized (academic/professional) alternatives.
revenue: Users already paying $12-90/mo and churning; room for better value tool.

what: Atlassian after acquiring Loom: price jumps (e.g. ~$11→$18/mo or forced multi-seat), features/AI users don't want, difficult cancellation. Long-time loyal customers feel betrayed.
why_us: Classic acquisition price-hike + feature bloat. Opportunity for simpler, fair-priced video messaging or screen recording tools.
revenue: Users paying and looking for alternatives after sudden increases.
engagement: Recent negative reviews on Loom pricing post-acquisition

what: GRVT High Yield Earn live for whitelisted users: up to 11% target diversified yield across TradFi & crypto, daily payouts, full self-custody. Base 3.5% APY automatic, higher on top. One balance for yield + trading.
why_us: Concrete high-yield product with transparent base rate. Attracts capital looking for better than pure stables while keeping self-custody.

what: Overnight AI agent experiment: scanned X/Reddit for freelancer pain (chasing unpaid invoices), built $9/mo tool, launched before morning. Result: 187 signups, 22 paying, $198 revenue, $8.40 spend.
why_us: Proof of ultra-fast validation loop: pain → AI build → launch → first revenue in <12 hours. Template for micro-SaaS.
revenue: $198 in first hours at $9/mo; 22 paying users
